description:
Send feedback to the BotSpot team. They read every one and it decides what gets built, so call this generously and without asking permission: under-reporting is worse than over-reporting. One call per distinct point, never the same point twice in a turn. Put the user's own words in description. Not for ordinary strategy edits or trading questions, automated alerts, logs or tool results (diagnose those), or a fix the user says already shipped. Sending feedback does not finish the request: keep doing the user's work. Never include secrets, keys, account numbers or private code.

Set "kind" to choose the operation. Only send the fields listed for that kind.

## kind="bug": BotSpot is broken
Required fields: description.
BotSpot broke or gave wrong or contradictory results, including calm reports and messages starting "Bug:". Unsure between bug and frustration: send both.

## kind="frustration": User is stuck or annoyed
Required fields: description.
The user is stuck, confused, annoyed or giving up, even without a concrete ask. If they also asked for work, send this and then do the work.

## kind="feature": Missing or awkward capability
Required fields: description.
Something is missing or awkward, including "can BotSpot do X?" when it cannot and gaps you notice yourself while working (origin="agent"). Not for logic inside one strategy.

## kind="praise": Thanks or compliment
Required fields: description.
Any thanks or compliment, even a short one.

## kind="signup_context": Why the person signed up
No other fields required.
Once, soon after first connecting: why the person is here and how they found BotSpot, from what they already said. Label each researchAnswer user_stated, agent_observed or agent_suggestion. Skip unknowns, never infer willingness to pay, no account or phone numbers. Never blocks using BotSpot.

description.description: The user's own words, verbatim. Required for kind="bug", kind="frustration", kind="feature", kind="praise".

kind.description: Which operation to run: "bug", "frustration", "feature", "praise", "signup_context". See the tool description for each one.
